dataset: Exploring the 5G Digital Divide in the Non-Contiguous US: LEO Satellites to the Rescue? — Maui, Hawaii road test, August 2024
limitations: Measurements are from mobile Maui drive tests, not disaster recovery, Hurricane Helene, North Carolina, or AI agents.
Ping contains only finite successful RTT measurements and has no sequence numbers, sent-probe count, or explicit failed-probe rows. Gaps cannot establish loss or outage duration.
Irregular sample intervals and long collection gaps remain. Do not interpolate across gaps; report temporal hold-out and the gap threshold.
Do not claim satellite-phase causality from timestamp predictability alone; shared load, mobility, route, and collection effects are confounders.
A trace replay or RTT forecast is a preliminary network experiment; it is not measured agent completion performance.

normalization.compression: Terminal CSV is gzip compressed with mtime=0 for deterministic output.
normalization.outages: Outage fields are retained as source telemetry. Repeated event fields are not independently verified current-state labels or packet-loss indicators.
normalization.ping_timestamp_semantics: Unknown whether source time labels probe send or reply. Conservatively make a finite RTT sample usable at timestamp_s + rtt_ms/1000. Absolute local_dt is trusted over inconsistent source utc_ts; cross-stream clock synchronization is not independently validated.
normalization.rows: All rows retained in original order. No interpolation, resampling, artificial loss rows, or imputation. source_row is 1-based original CSV data-row number.
normalization.source_session: Constant campaign identifier; not an uninterrupted run. Split at gaps before time-series prediction.
normalization.terminal_timestamp_semantics: Source local_dt equals response time in inspected rows; canonical timestamp is parsed local_dt. Explicit gRPC request and response times are retained. Terminal latency_ms is a vendor-reported metric, not ICMP RTT or an application request service time.
normalization.throughput: Terminal tput_dl_bps and tput_ul_bps are measured achieved traffic rates, retained only as raw context; they do not estimate available service capacity.
normalization.timestamp_quality_warning: Every ping source utc_ts is exactly 36000 seconds earlier than offset-aware local_dt; terminal source utc_ts is milliseconds, truncated to integer milliseconds. source_utc_ts is preserved unmodified in both outputs.
normalization.timestamp_s: Unix UTC seconds derived from offset-aware source local_dt, retaining microseconds.
